correctness.rationale: The degree filtration kills the fourth power. Expanding the commuting left and right multiplication operators gives the three rows of the second power and the sole row of the third; the latter has coefficients -BCD, 3ACD, -3ABD, ABC. Thus the characteristic-three exception is exact, not a size-three-field artifact. For the nonadjacent two-support masks the only variable pivots are the stipulated linear forms (and the private -2AD pivot); for 1011 and 1101 the lower-degree rows are collinear and the remaining row has a private pivot. The other masks follow from the displayed disjoint pivots. Normalizing the four first-superdiagonal entries by diagonal conjugation is valid on the path of five vertices. Summing the support weights recovers all five rows; in particular the two exceptional three-support masks move 2q^6(q-1)^3 from (2,1) to (2,0) in characteristic three. The nilpotent block identities and squarefree monomial component decomposition give the advertised consequences.
residual_risks: The fresh enumeration covers F_3 only; uniformity is from the symbolic proof. The bundled verifier specifies replays at q=2,3,4,5, but its recorded outputs are not independent executions in this review.
The geometric claim is about reduced components, not scheme multiplicities; the counted ranks do not determine blocks of lengths one or two.

value.rationale: The last two nonzero powers in this small nilradical distinguish co-occurrence from mere existence of the two longest Jordan blocks. A complete field-uniform law locating the characteristic-three failure of (2,1) and giving the frequencies of all alternatives is useful as a baseline for larger triangular sizes and cannot be inferred from either the maximal-block count or the first-power spectrum.
residual_risks: Value is for the precise long-block law, not a claim of a full Jordan classification or a new general maximal-chain theorem.
